note: Disability help outside the United States, built into world.html and countries/<slug>.html by scripts/build_world_pages.py. Added November 19, 2026 at the owner's request (Jamaica, Kenya, Mexico and Nigeria added November 20, 2026; Bangladesh, Barbados, the Bahamas, Ghana, Malaysia, Pakistan, Singapore, Tanzania, Trinidad and Tobago, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe added November 21, 2026; Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Peru, Poland and Spain added the same day): Mobility Talk is to become global, not only U.S. Every listing names the pages it was checked against and the date. 'phone' is printed the way the country writes it; 'dial' is the digits a phone in that country dials, or a full +country number for a line called from abroad. A listing taken from a directory or news page rather than the program's own page carries record_status 'directory_listed' and shows the confirm-details note. The crisis lines and emergency numbers were checked the same day for Yoga Mom Talk's worldwide pages and are kept in step with them. A 'dial' that starts with * is a mobile short code, such as Chile's *4141.

sections.help-now: Crisis and someone to talk to
sections.equipment-home: Equipment, home changes and getting around

worldwide.name: Find A Helpline
worldwide.what: A free directory of crisis and support lines in more than 130 countries. Pick your country and what you want to talk about, and it shows lines you can call, text or chat with.
worldwide.how: Choose your country on the site. Most lines are free and many are open any hour.

worldwide.name: Be My Eyes
worldwide.what: A free app for people who are blind or have low vision. A sighted volunteer looks through your phone's camera and tells you what they see, or an AI describes a photo. The company says it works in about 150 countries and 180 languages.
worldwide.how: Download the app, choose your language, and start a video call or send a photo. It is free.

worldwide.name: U.S. citizens abroad: emergency help
worldwide.what: For Americans living or traveling outside the U.S. The State Department helps U.S. citizens abroad with emergencies, including crime, arrest and lost passports.
worldwide.how: Contact the nearest U.S. embassy, or call any hour. From the U.S. and Canada, call 1-888-407-4747.
worldwide.phone_note: From outside the U.S. and Canada, any hour

countries.name: Australia
countries.relay: Deaf, hard of hearing or speech disability: use the National Relay Service. Call 133 677 (TTY or voice) or 1300 555 727 (Speak and Listen) and ask for the number you need.

resources.name: Lifeline crisis support
resources.what: Free, confidential crisis support any hour for anyone in Australia who feels overwhelmed, is in emotional distress or is thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call, text 0477 13 11 14, or chat online. Through TIS on 131 450 you can ask for Lifeline in your language.

resources.name: Disability Gateway
resources.org: Australian Government Department of Social Services
resources.what: A free, Australia-wide information line for people with disability, families and carers. A real person helps you find services for income, equipment, housing, transport, work, health and rights, and can transfer you to counselling or advocacy. Anyone can call, whether or not they are on the NDIS.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm (AEST/AEDT). For another language, call TIS on 131 450 and ask for the Disability Gateway.

resources.name: National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS)
resources.what: The national scheme that funds supports for people with permanent and significant disability. The NDIS can help you apply, or connect you with a local partner who will.
resources.how: Call the participant line Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm local time, or use the webchat. First Nations Connect: 1800 411 640.

resources.name: Australian Human Rights Commission: disability discrimination complaints
resources.what: Looks into and helps resolve complaints about disability discrimination under the Disability Discrimination Act. Making a complaint is free, and someone such as an advocate can complain for you.
resources.how: Call the National Information Service if you are not sure you can complain, or lodge a complaint online. Through the National Relay Service, ask to be connected to the Commission. For an interpreter, call TIS on 131 450.

resources.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.what: Call or text 9-8-8 any hour, anywhere in Canada, if you are thinking about suicide or are worried about someone. Free, in English and French.
resources.how: Call or text 988. If 988 does not work on your phone, call 1-833-456-4566.

resources.name: Canada Disability Benefit
resources.what: A monthly payment for working-age people with disabilities, 18 to 64, who have low income. You must already be approved for the Disability Tax Credit.
resources.how: Apply online, by phone, or at a Service Canada Centre. If you do not have the Disability Tax Credit yet, apply for it first through the Canada Revenue Agency. TTY: 1-833-467-2700.

resources.name: Canada Pension Plan disability benefits
resources.what: A monthly payment if you paid into the Canada Pension Plan and can no longer work regularly at any job because of a severe and prolonged disability. Your children may also get benefits.
resources.how: Apply online, or call for an application kit. TTY: 1-800-255-4786. From outside Canada and the United States, call collect 1-613-957-1954.

resources.name: Canadian Human Rights Commission
resources.what: Takes discrimination complaints against federally regulated organizations, such as federal government departments, banks, airlines and phone companies. For other employers, landlords, stores and services, complain to your province's or territory's human rights agency. Filing is free and you do not need a lawyer.
resources.how: Call to check that the Commission is the right place, then fill in its complaint form. Lines are open Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm Eastern. TTY: 1-888-643-3304.

resources.name: Tele-MANAS mental health helpline
resources.org: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
resources.what: Free mental health support by phone any hour, from the national tele-mental health programme, in many Indian languages.

resources.name: Disability certificate and UDID card
resources.org: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: One national disability certificate and Unique Disability ID card, issued under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Many schemes ask for it, including free or low-cost aids and devices under ADIP.
resources.how: Apply free on the Swavlamban card portal: register, choose a government hospital in your district, and attend the medical assessment there. You can track your application on the same site.

resources.name: ADIP scheme: aids and assistive devices
resources.org: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Government help to buy or be fitted with aids and assistive devices, given through ALIMCO, the National Institutes, Composite Regional Centres, District Disability Rehabilitation Centres and other implementing agencies. A UDID card is required.
resources.how: Apply through one of those agencies or register on the ADIP portal. For replacement or repair of a device from ALIMCO, call its toll-free line.
resources.phone_note: ALIMCO toll-free, for replacement or repair

resources.name: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
resources.org: Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)
resources.what: Takes complaints when a person with a disability is denied rights under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, for example by a government body or employer. Each state also has a State Commissioner.
resources.how: Send a written complaint by email or post, or bring it in person. Say who you are, what happened, where, and which organization it was.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance (999 works too). Free from any phone

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.what: Someone to talk to, free, any time of day or night, whatever you are going through. You do not have to be suicidal to call.
resources.how: Call 116 123 from any phone.

resources.name: Citizens Information Phone Service
resources.what: Free, confidential information on public services and entitlements, including disability payments, grants and services. Local Citizens Information Centres can also help you fill in forms.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday, 9am to 8pm. Calls cost the same as a landline call. From outside Ireland, call +353 21 229 8178.

resources.name: Disability Allowance
resources.what: A weekly payment for people aged 16 to 65 with a disability expected to last at least a year that substantially limits the work they can do. It is means tested, and you must live in Ireland. You can keep attending school while you get it.
resources.how: Fill in the application form on the gov.ie page, or get one at your Intreo centre or Citizens Information Centre, and send it with your supporting documents to the Disability Allowance Section.

resources.name: Housing Adaptation Grant for Disabled People
resources.org: Your local authority (county or city council)
resources.what: A means-tested grant toward changes that make a private home suitable for a disabled person, such as access and moving around inside. The maximum grant is €40,000. Social housing tenants use a separate scheme run by their council.
resources.how: Get the application form from your local authority's housing grants page or office, have your doctor complete the medical section, and return it to the council.

resources.name: National Advocacy Service for People with Disabilities
resources.what: An independent, confidential and free advocacy service. An advocate can speak up for you or help you be heard when dealing with services.
resources.how: Call or email info@advocacy.ie. For discrimination at work or in services, IHREC's Your Rights pages explain the law; complaints go to the Workplace Relations Commission.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.relay: Deaf, hard of hearing or speech disability: use New Zealand Relay to reach any number listed here.

resources.name: 1737, Need to talk?
resources.what: Free call or text any hour to talk with a trained counsellor, or with a peer support worker, about feeling down, anxious or overwhelmed.
resources.how: Call or text 1737.

resources.name: Disability Support Services
resources.what: The government's disability support service, including needs assessment (through NASC), Enabling Good Lives, carer support, and equipment and modification services. Your first point of contact is usually your provider, your NASC or your Enabling Good Lives site.
resources.how: Call Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 8am to 5pm, Wednesday 9:30am to 5pm, or email info@disabilitysupport.govt.nz.

resources.name: Work and Income: Disability Allowance and Supported Living Payment
resources.org: Work and Income (Ministry of Social Development)
resources.what: Disability Allowance is a weekly payment for regular, ongoing costs because of a disability; you do not have to be on a benefit to get it. Supported Living Payment is for people permanently and severely restricted in their ability to work because of a health condition, injury or disability, or who are totally blind.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday 7am to 6pm, or Saturday 8am to 1pm. A health practitioner fills in a medical certificate for either payment.

resources.name: Te Kāhui Tika Tangata Human Rights Commission
resources.what: A free, confidential information and dispute resolution service for discrimination complaints, including disability discrimination under the Human Rights Act 1993.
resources.how: Call the InfoLine or use the online form on the Commission's website.

resources.name: NCMH Crisis Hotline
resources.what: The government's mental health crisis line, open any hour, for anyone in emotional distress or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Dial 1553 toll-free from a landline. From a mobile, call 0919 057 1553 (Smart/TNT) or 0917 899 8727 (Globe/TM).

resources.name: PWD ID card
resources.org: Your city or municipality (PDAO), with the National Council on Disability Affairs
resources.what: The identification card for persons with disability. Under Republic Act 10754 it gives at least a 20% discount and VAT exemption on many goods and services, such as medicines and medical and dental services. It is registered in the Philippine Registry for Persons with Disabilities.
resources.how: Apply at the Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO) or the social welfare office of your city or municipality, with the application form and a certificate of disability from a doctor where the disability is not apparent. To report a fake PWD ID, email NCDA.

resources.name: AICS medical and assistive device help
resources.org: Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD)
resources.what: Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) gives one-time financial help to people facing a crisis, including medical help that can cover medicine and assistive devices. DSWD says it is not only for the poor.
resources.how: Go to a DSWD Crisis Intervention Unit or your local social welfare office with a valid ID, a medical certificate or clinical abstract, a prescription or request for the device, and a price quotation. A social worker assesses your situation.
resources.phone_note: DSWD Crisis Intervention Unit, Quezon City, weekdays 8am to 5pm

resources.name: Commission on Human Rights
resources.org: Commission on Human Rights of the Philippines
resources.what: The national human rights institution. It takes complaints and gives legal help, and monitors the rights of persons with disabilities under the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability and the UN disability rights convention.
resources.how: Call the head office (press 2) or its Public Assistance and Complaints Desk on 0936 068 0982 (Globe) or 0920 506 1194 (Smart), or email publicassistance@chr.gov.ph.

resources.name: Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.org: South African Depression and Anxiety Group
resources.what: A toll-free crisis line, open any hour, for anyone thinking about suicide or worried about someone.
resources.how: Call toll-free from any network.

resources.name: Disability Grant
resources.what: A monthly grant if a physical or mental disability makes you unfit to work for more than six months. It is temporary (6 to 12 months) or permanent, depending on a medical assessment by a SASSA doctor. A caregiver of a child under 18 who needs permanent care can apply for the Care Dependency Grant instead.
resources.how: Apply in person at your nearest SASSA office; the form is not online. Bring your ID and any medical reports. Applying is free. Email: GrantEnquiries@sassa.gov.za.

resources.name: Care Dependency Grant
resources.what: A monthly grant for the parent or caregiver of a child under 18 with a severe disability who needs full-time care. It is means tested, and a medical assessment must confirm the disability.
resources.how: Apply free at your nearest SASSA office with your ID, the child's birth certificate and the medical reports. Forms are not online.

resources.name: South African Human Rights Commission
resources.what: Takes complaints about human rights violations, including against people with disabilities, which is one of its focus areas. Complaining is free, and there are offices in all nine provinces.
resources.how: Use the online complaint form, email complaints@sahrc.org.za, call the head office, or visit a provincial office.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.relay: Deaf, hard of hearing or speech disability: with Relay UK, dial 18001 and then the number you need.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.what: Someone to talk to, free, any time of day or night, from any phone. You do not have to be suicidal to call.

resources.name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
resources.what: A tax-free benefit for people aged 16 or over who have not reached State Pension age, to help with the extra costs of long-term ill health or disability. Older people claim Attendance Allowance, and children under 16 get Disability Living Allowance.
resources.how: Start a claim by phone, Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm, or online in some areas. Relay UK: 18001 then 0800 917 2222. From abroad: +44 191 218 7766. In Scotland, apply for Adult Disability Payment instead; Northern Ireland has its own claim line on nidirect.

resources.name: Adult Disability Payment (Scotland)
resources.what: Scotland's benefit for disabled working-age adults, in place of PIP, to help with the extra costs of a disability or long-term health condition.
resources.how: Apply online at mygov.scot, or call free to apply by phone and paper form. British Sign Language users can call through Contact Scotland BSL.

resources.name: Disabled Facilities Grant
resources.what: A council grant toward changes to your home so you can keep living there. Up to £30,000 in England, £36,000 in Wales and £25,000 in Northern Ireland. Not available in Scotland. It usually depends on household income and savings, but disabled children under 18 can get one without their parents' income being counted.
resources.how: Apply to your council. Do not start the work before the council approves your application, or you might not get any grant.

resources.name: Blue Badge parking
resources.what: Parking help for disabled people with severe walking difficulties who travel as drivers or passengers. A badge costs up to £10 in England and £20 in Scotland, is free in Wales, and usually lasts up to 3 years.
resources.how: Apply online; your council decides, usually within 12 weeks. Have a recent digital photo, proof of identity and address, and proof of any benefits ready. Northern Ireland has its own way to apply on nidirect.

resources.name: Access to Work
resources.what: Help to get or stay in work if you have a physical or mental health condition or disability. It can pay for specialist equipment, support workers, travel to work, vehicle adaptations, workplace changes, mental health support and communication support at job interviews.
resources.how: Check eligibility and apply on GOV.UK.

resources.name: Equality Advisory Support Service (EASS)
resources.what: A free helpline on discrimination and your rights under the Equality Act 2010, for England, Scotland and Wales. It can explain the law, help you try to resolve the problem informally, and tell you about your options.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday 9am to 7pm, or Saturday 10am to 2pm. Textphone: 0808 800 0084. There is also a contact form and BSL interpretation on the EASS website.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance or the fire service, dial 110

resources.name: Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Helpline (888-NEW-LIFE)
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's free helpline for anyone in Jamaica who is struggling, including anyone thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call 888-NEW-LIFE (888-639-5433). It is toll-free.

resources.name: Register with the Jamaica Council for Persons with Disabilities (JCPD)
resources.org: Jamaica Council for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: The government agency for people with disabilities. Registering is what opens its grants and services, and only registered members get benefits such as disability parking stickers and access to the share of National Housing Trust homes set aside for people with disabilities.
resources.how: Register through the I Am Able: My JCPD app (Android), at the JCPD head office at 1C-1F Pawsey Road, Kingston 5, or with a social worker at a Ministry of Labour and Social Security parish office. Call 876-515-9069 or 876-447-0444, or email jcpd@jcpd.gov.jm.

resources.name: JCPD Assistive Aid and Economic Empowerment grants
resources.org: Jamaica Council for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Registered members, or their caregivers, can apply for help buying assistive aids such as wheelchairs, hearing aids, white canes and prostheses, and for grants to start a small business. In June 2026 the JCPD said assistive aid help runs up to J$300,000 and business grants from J$50,000 to J$250,000, depending on the need.
resources.how: Register with the JCPD first, then apply in the I Am Able: My JCPD app or at a JCPD or parish office.

resources.name: Discrimination complaints and the Disabilities Rights Tribunal
resources.org: Jamaica Council for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Under the Disabilities Act, 2014 (in force since 2022), you can complain to the JCPD about disability discrimination. The JCPD investigates and tries mediation; if that does not settle it, the case goes to the Disabilities Rights Tribunal, which decides it.
resources.how: Make a written complaint to the JCPD on its complaint form, in person, by email to jcpd@jcpd.gov.jm, or in the I Am Able: My JCPD app. There is a time limit, so complain soon after it happens.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. 112 and 911 also work

resources.name: Kenya Red Cross 1199
resources.what: A free 24-hour line run by the Kenya Red Cross. Its counsellors give emotional and psychosocial support to people in distress.
resources.how: Dial 1199. If it does not connect, call the Red Cross on +254 703 037 000.

resources.name: Register with the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD)
resources.org: National Council for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Registration with NCPWD is free and is the key to its services: assistive devices, education help, economic empowerment grants, job placement, legal advice and the income tax exemption. You need a disability assessment report from a government-gazetted hospital, signed by the county medical director.
resources.how: Get assessed at a gazetted hospital, then register on eCitizen (ncpwd.ecitizen.go.ke) with the report, your national ID or a child's birth certificate, and a passport photo. Or ask at your county NCPWD office.

resources.name: Inua Jamii cash transfer for persons with severe disabilities
resources.what: Regular payments to households caring for a person with a severe disability who needs permanent care, through the Inua Jamii programme. Recipients must not be in another government cash transfer programme.
resources.how: Ask your local social development officer about enrolment, or email inuajamii@socialprotection.go.ke. Paid recipients can check and withdraw funds by dialling *222#.

resources.name: NCPWD assistive devices
resources.org: National Council for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Registered members can apply for assistive devices, including motorized wheelchairs. For a motorized wheelchair, NCPWD covers up to KES 100,000 and you pay anything above that.
resources.how: Fill in the assistive device form, get a recommendation from the right professional (a physiotherapist or orthopaedic technologist, an audiologist, or an ophthalmologist), attach your NCPWD card, ID and assessment report, and hand it in at your county NCPWD office.

resources.name: Income tax exemption for persons with disabilities
resources.org: National Council for Persons with Disabilities, with the Kenya Revenue Authority
resources.what: Registered persons with disabilities who have taxable income can be exempted from tax on the first KES 150,000 of income a month.
resources.how: Apply through the NCPWD portal on eCitizen with your NCPWD certificate, KRA PIN, a valid tax compliance certificate and the other listed documents. NCPWD says it takes one to three months.

resources.name: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights
resources.org: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights
resources.what: Takes complaints about human rights violations, including against persons with disabilities. It monitors Kenya's duties under the UN disability rights convention and the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2025.
resources.how: Call the toll-free line and say you want to lodge a complaint; the Commission calls you back at its cost. You can also SMS 22359, email complaints@knchr.org, or complain on the website.

emergency.label: Police, fire and medical emergencies across the country

resources.name: Línea de la Vida
resources.org: Comisión Nacional de Salud Mental y Adicciones (CONASAMA)
resources.what: Mexico's free national line for anyone in emotional crisis, thinking about suicide, or dealing with addiction, open any hour.
resources.how: Call 800 911 2000 from any phone in Mexico. The line is in Spanish.

resources.name: Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas con Discapacidad Permanente
resources.what: A federal pension paid every two months to people with a permanent disability. In states that signed agreements with the federal government it covers ages 0 to 64; elsewhere the age range is narrower. At 65, recipients move to the older adults' pension.
resources.how: Registration opens at set times at Módulos del Bienestar (find yours at ubicatumodulo.bienestar.gob.mx). Bring a birth certificate, official ID, CURP, recent proof of address and, where your state asks for it, a disability certificate. For questions, call the Línea del Bienestar.
resources.phone_note: Línea del Bienestar: weekdays 8:00 to 21:00, weekends and holidays 9:00 to 13:00

resources.name: DIF rehabilitation centres (CRI, CREE and UBR)
resources.org: Sistema Nacional DIF and state and municipal DIF systems
resources.what: The DIF family-services system runs rehabilitation centres across the country: Centros de Rehabilitación Integral (CRI), Centros de Rehabilitación y Educación Especial (CREE) and local Unidades Básicas de Rehabilitación (UBR). They offer therapy and rehabilitation for people with temporary or permanent disabilities, and many help with functional aids.
resources.how: Ask your municipal or state DIF office for the nearest CRI, CREE or UBR. Services and costs are set by each state.

resources.name: CONAPRED: discrimination complaints
resources.org: Consejo Nacional para Prevenir la Discriminación
resources.what: The national council against discrimination. It takes complaints when a person, business or public office treats you unfairly because of a disability, and disability is one of the most common reasons people complain to it.
resources.how: Call toll-free from outside Mexico City (in the city, 55 5262 1490), Monday to Thursday 9:00 to 17:30 and Friday 9:00 to 15:00, or file a complaint online.

emergency.label: National emergency number, free from any network

resources.name: She Writes Woman mental health helpline
resources.what: A free mental health line for anyone in Nigeria who is struggling emotionally.

resources.name: National Commission for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD)
resources.org: National Commission for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: The federal agency set up by the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act, 2018. It registers persons with disabilities, links them to social protection programmes, promotes affordable assistive technology and takes up cases where the Act is not being followed, including discrimination.
resources.how: Call or email the Commission, or visit its head office at Plot 79 Ralph Shodeinde Street, Central Business District, Abuja.

resources.name: National Human Rights Commission
resources.what: Takes complaints about human rights violations, free of charge, at its headquarters and state offices, including violations against persons with disabilities.
resources.how: Call the toll-free line or the short code 6472, file a complaint online, or write to the Executive Secretary at any NHRC office.

countries.name: Singapore

emergency.label: Ambulance and fire. For the police, call 999

countries.relay: Deaf, hard of hearing or speech-impaired: text 70995 for an ambulance or fire engine, or text 70999 for the police when it is not safe to talk.

resources.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
resources.what: A 24-hour hotline for anyone in crisis, in distress or thinking about suicide. Its CareText service on WhatsApp is also open at any hour.
resources.how: Call 1767. To write instead, send a WhatsApp message to 9151 1767.

resources.name: SG Enable and the Enabling Guide
resources.what: SG Enable runs several of Singapore's disability schemes, including the Assistive Technology Fund and the Taxi Subsidy Scheme. Its Enabling Guide website lists the schemes for assistive technology, transport, care and work in one place.
resources.how: Call the hotline on weekdays, 9am to 5.30pm, or email contactus@sgenable.sg.

resources.name: Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)
resources.what: Pays up to 90% of the cost of devices such as wheelchairs and hearing aids, including repairs, upgrades and replacements, up to S$40,000 in a lifetime. It is for Singapore citizens and permanent residents with a permanent disability and a monthly household income of S$4,800 or less per person.
resources.how: A therapist or social worker at a public hospital or social service agency assesses what you need and applies for you. If no one is looking after you yet, ask a polyclinic to refer you to a public hospital.

resources.name: Taxi Subsidy Scheme
resources.what: Pays part of taxi fares to school, work or SG Enable-supported training for people with a permanent physical, visual or intellectual disability, or autism, who cannot use public transport. It is for citizens and permanent residents with a monthly household income of S$4,800 or less per person who do not own a vehicle.
resources.how: Apply online with Singpass, or email the form and documents to tss@sgenable.sg. SG Enable says it decides within 15 working days of getting everything.

resources.name: Persons with Disabilities Concession Card
resources.what: Up to 55% off adult bus and train fares, plus monthly passes for unlimited travel, for citizens and permanent residents aged 7 to under 60 with a verified permanent disability.
resources.how: Check on SupportGoWhere, with Singpass, whether your disability is already verified. If not, have a registered healthcare professional fill in a Disability Verification Form and submit it there. Then apply through SimplyGo.

resources.name: Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP)
resources.what: Helps workers who face discrimination at work, including because of a disability or a mental health condition. If it finds discrimination, it refers the employer to the Ministry of Manpower. The Workplace Fairness Act, which covers disability, is due to take effect by the end of 2027.
resources.how: Try your employer's grievance process or your union first. If that does not fix it, report it on TAFEP's online form, or call on weekdays, 8.30am to 5.30pm; an officer may call you back.

resources.name: Disabled People's Association (DPA)
resources.what: A cross-disability advocacy group led by and for people with disabilities. It speaks to decision-makers on disability policy and runs access guides and disability awareness training.
resources.how: Call or email to ask for help or to join as a member.

emergency.label: Police, fire and rescue, health and civil defence. Free

resources.name: Befrienders Kuala Lumpur
resources.what: A free, private listening line, open 24 hours a day, every day, for anyone who feels lonely, in distress or is thinking about suicide.

resources.name: Talian HEAL 15555
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's counselling line for emotional support and early crisis help, including for suicidal thoughts, depression, anxiety and stress. It is open every day from 8am to midnight.
resources.how: Dial 15555. Your mobile carrier may charge for the call.

resources.name: Register as a person with disabilities (OKU)
resources.what: Malaysian citizens with a permanent physical, mental, learning, hearing, speech, vision or multiple disability, confirmed by a medical specialist, can register as OKU with the Social Welfare Department (JKM).
resources.how: Get a report from a medical specialist at a government or private hospital or clinic. Then apply online through MyDaftar OKU, or take the BPPOKU form, the report and a copy of your MyKad (or a child's birth certificate) to a JKM counter.

resources.name: PERKESO Invalidity Scheme
resources.what: For insured employees who become permanently unable to earn a living because of an illness or injury from any cause, not only at work, as decided by a PERKESO Medical Board. It pays a monthly pension of 50% to 65% of average wages (at least RM475), RM500 a month more if you need someone with you at all times, and covers rehabilitation and aids such as wheelchairs, crutches, hearing aids and artificial limbs.
resources.how: Ask PERKESO about making an invalidity claim.

resources.name: Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (SUHAKAM)
resources.what: Malaysia's national human rights commission. It takes complaints about human rights violations through its online complaint system.
resources.how: Complain online, call the Kuala Lumpur office on weekdays, or email humanrights@suhakam.org.my.

resources.name: National Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Helpline
resources.what: A free 24-hour line from Ghana's Mental Health Authority, where you can talk to a counsellor about any mental health worry, including thoughts of suicide.
resources.how: Call 0800 678 678. It is toll-free.

resources.name: National Council on Persons with Disability (NCPD)
resources.org: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection
resources.what: The government body set up under the Persons with Disability Act, 2006 (Act 715) to shape disability policy. It keeps the national register of persons with disability and of the organisations that serve them.
resources.how: Contact the Ministry, which the Council sits under, to ask about registering.
resources.phone_note: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection

resources.name: Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ)
resources.what: Takes complaints about human rights violations, including discrimination, free of charge. Complain within 12 months of what happened.
resources.how: Call the toll-free line, email info@chraj.gov.gh, or visit any CHRAJ office, weekdays 8am to 6pm. To report discrimination from any phone without data or credit, dial *920*59#; a case officer calls back within 48 hours.

resources.name: Ghana Federation of Disability Organisations (GFD)
resources.what: The national umbrella of organisations of persons with disabilities, set up in 1987. It advocates for disability rights and helps its member organisations grow.
resources.how: Call its toll-free number.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. 112 also works

resources.name: Mental Health Uganda toll-free line
resources.what: Free, confidential support from trained counsellors for anyone struggling with their mental health, with information and referrals to further care. You can talk in several local languages.
resources.how: Call 0800 21 21 21, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm. At other times, in an emergency, call 999.

resources.name: Special Grant for Persons with Disabilities
resources.org: Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development
resources.what: Grants for money-making projects run by groups of 5 to 15 people in the same sub-county: persons with disabilities aged 15 and over, carers of children with disabilities, or registered homes for persons with disabilities. Groups have used it for things like rearing animals, mobile money and buying and selling produce.
resources.how: Plan the project as a group, fill in the disability grant project application form, and hand it in at your sub-county through the community development officer.

resources.name: Equal Opportunities Commission
resources.what: Investigates and tries to settle complaints of discrimination, including because of disability. Complain within six months of what happened.
resources.how: Use the online complaint form, call the toll-free line, or email info@eoc.go.ug.

resources.name: National Union of Disabled Persons of Uganda (NUDIPU)
resources.what: The national umbrella of organisations of persons with disabilities, formed in 1987. Its members are 146 district unions and 17 national disability organisations. It advocates for disability rights and runs training, business and job programmes.
resources.how: Call or email NUDIPU, or ask your district union of persons with disabilities.

resources.name: Ministry of Health line 199
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's free line, which has a psychological support desk where you can get counselling. Most information is in Swahili.
resources.how: Call 199 for free, or send a text message to 15061.

resources.name: National Child Helpline 116
resources.what: A free, confidential line open 24 hours for children and young people, and for adults worried about a child.
resources.how: Call 116, or send a WhatsApp message to +255 624 100 100.

resources.name: Tanzania Federation of Disabled People's Organisations (SHIVYAWATA)
resources.what: The national federation of organisations of persons with disabilities. It speaks for disabled people on policy and law.
resources.how: Call or email the federation in Dar es Salaam.

resources.name: Tanzania League of the Blind
resources.what: A national membership organisation for people with visual impairment. It advocates for their rights and supports education, assistive technology, digital skills and job training.
resources.how: Call or email, Monday to Saturday, 9am to 6pm. The office is on Chui Street, Kariakoo, Dar es Salaam.

resources.name: Lifeline Zambia 933
resources.what: A free 24-hour counselling line. Lifeline/Childline Zambia also does crisis support and suicide prevention work. Children can call Childline on 116.
resources.how: Call 933. It is toll-free.

resources.name: Zambia Agency for Persons with Disabilities (ZAPD)
resources.org: Zambia Agency for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: The government agency set up under the Persons with Disabilities Act, 2012. It keeps the national register of persons with disabilities and can run schemes for self-employment and jobs.
resources.how: Contact the head office on Leopards Hill Road, Lusaka, to register or to ask about its programmes.

resources.name: Human Rights Commission
resources.what: Investigates human rights complaints for free, including from persons with disabilities. The Persons with Disabilities Act, 2012 bans discrimination because of disability.
resources.how: Call the toll-free line 8181 from Airtel, MTN or Zamtel, send a WhatsApp message to 0954 443 010, email complaints@hrc.org.zm, or visit a provincial office.

resources.name: Youth Advocates Zimbabwe helpline 393
resources.what: A free 24-hour line where young people can talk to peers about suicide, depression, stress, abuse and other worries.
resources.how: Dial 393 from any mobile network, or call 0777 469 107. Children can also call Childline on 116.

resources.name: Zimbabwe Human Rights Commission
resources.what: Takes and investigates complaints about human rights violations. The Persons with Disabilities Act, passed in 2025, bans discrimination because of disability and requires reasonable accommodation.
resources.how: Lodge a complaint on the website, email info@zhrc.org.zw, or call on weekdays, 8am to 5pm.

resources.name: Rozan Counseling Helpline
resources.what: Telephone counselling for emotional and mental health worries, with referrals to other services. Rozan also offers counselling in person, especially for women and children, and by email.
resources.how: Call 0304 111 1741, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm, or email helpline@rozan.org. In an emergency, call 1122 or 15.

resources.name: Identity card with the disability logo (NADRA)
resources.what: NADRA issues identity cards (CNICs) to persons with disabilities that carry the international disability logo and are valid for life. Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal accepts this card as proof of disability.
resources.how: Apply at a NADRA office. NADRA has said persons with disabilities are served without queueing and that it offers registration at home.

resources.name: Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal: help for families with a person with disabilities
resources.what: Yearly cash help for families with a person with disabilities: Rs. 20,000 a year for one person with disabilities, Rs. 30,000 for two or more.
resources.how: Fill in the PBM application form and attach a copy of the CNIC (or a child's B-Form) and a disability certificate or a NADRA CNIC with the disability logo.

resources.name: Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal: wheelchairs and assistive devices
resources.what: Standard and customised wheelchairs, hearing aids, white canes and artificial limbs. People aged 60 and over can also get a standard wheelchair.
resources.how: Apply with a CNIC copy and a disability certificate. A standard wheelchair needs a government medical officer's recommendation; hearing aids and artificial limbs need an estimate from a government hospital. In some districts, including Islamabad, customised wheelchairs are applied for online.

resources.name: Punjab Assistive Devices and Wheelchair Program
resources.org: Social Welfare and Bait-ul-Maal Department, Punjab
resources.what: For residents of Punjab: wheelchairs, prosthetics, orthotics and other assistive devices, fitted to each person after an assessment.
resources.how: Apply on the program's website or app, or at your nearest Social Welfare and Bait-ul-Maal office. You need a CNIC or B-Form and a Disability Assessment Certificate. For wheelchairs and artificial limbs, an orthopaedic specialist at a DHQ or teaching hospital assesses what you need.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. Free, any hour

resources.name: Kaan Pete Roi
resources.what: Bangladesh's emotional support and suicide prevention helpline. Trained volunteers listen in confidence to anyone in despair, alone or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call 09612 119911 any day from 3pm to 3am, except on holidays. In an emergency, call 999.

resources.name: Disability identification and ID card
resources.what: Under the Rights and Protection of Persons with Disabilities Act 2013, persons with disabilities are registered and given an identity card after a medical check. The card helps you join government programmes.
resources.how: Apply online at dis.gov.bd, or take the form to the Upazila or City Social Service Office where you live. You need a birth registration or national ID card, a mobile number and an email address. The office sets a date for the medical check and sends an SMS when your card is ready.

resources.name: Disability allowance
resources.org: Department of Social Services, Ministry of Social Welfare
resources.what: A monthly allowance for persons with disabilities on low incomes who are over six years old. Local committees choose who gets it, with priority for older people, homeless people, women with multiple disabilities and poor children with intellectual disabilities.
resources.how: Ask at your Upazila Social Service Office.

resources.name: Lifeline Trinidad and Tobago
resources.what: A free listening line, open 24 hours, for anyone in distress or thinking about suicide. The Ministry of Health lists it among its suicide help numbers.
resources.how: Call 800-5588 or 866-5433, both toll-free.

resources.name: Disability Assistance Grant
resources.org: Government of Trinidad and Tobago (social welfare)
resources.what: A monthly grant for adults 18 and over who are certified as permanently disabled and unable to work, have an income of no more than TT$12,000 a year, and have lived in Trinidad and Tobago for at least 3 years. A separate grant pays TT$1,500 a month for children under 18 with a disability.
resources.how: Get the forms at your Local Board (Social Welfare) Office. Adults need a medical report from a Government Medical Officer, national ID, birth certificate and a bank statement. For general help, call ttconnect on weekdays, 8am to 4pm.

resources.name: Equal Opportunity Commission
resources.what: Takes complaints of discrimination because of disability, among other grounds, in jobs, education, goods and services, and housing. Complain in writing within six months of what happened.
resources.how: Use the online complaint form, email the form to complaints@eoc.gov.tt, or drop it at the office at 55-57 Manic Street, Chaguanas.

resources.name: Lifeline Barbados
resources.what: A 24-hour mental health helpline run by the Ministry of Health and Wellness.

resources.name: Register with the National Disabilities Unit
resources.what: The government unit for persons with disabilities uses its register to plan policies and programmes. Adults must be registered with it to use Call-A-Ride, which takes persons with disabilities to hospital appointments.
resources.how: Call 310-1650 and leave your contact details. Unit staff, carrying Unit picture IDs, will visit you to take the rest.

resources.name: Barbados Council for the Disabled
resources.what: Helps people with all kinds of disabilities. Its services include accessible transport, sign language interpreters, Braille translation, beach wheelchairs and checks of how accessible a property is.
resources.how: Call the Council. It is at Harambee House, The Garrison, St Michael.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. 911 also works

resources.name: Bahamas Crisis Centre
resources.what: A 24-hour hotline, answered by volunteers, for women, men and children facing domestic violence, abuse or any other crisis.

resources.name: Department of Social Services
resources.what: The government department whose work includes services for persons with disabilities. Its Disability Affairs Division helps persons with disabilities and their families.
resources.how: Call the Department, or visit it at Aventura Plaza, John F. Kennedy Drive and Bethel Avenue, Nassau.

resources.name: National Commission for Persons with Disabilities
resources.org: National Commission for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: The national commission for persons with disabilities. Its AccessAbility app lets you register with the Commission for free and has a way to make complaints.
resources.how: Call or send a WhatsApp message to the Commission's line, or email Disabilitiescommission@bahamas.gov.bs.

emergency.label: Ambulance and fire brigade. For the police, call 110

resources.name: TelefonSeelsorge
resources.what: A free, anonymous listening line for anyone in crisis or emotional distress, open around the clock. You can also write by email or chat.
resources.how: Call 0800 111 0 111 or 0800 111 0 222, or the European number 116 123. The service is in German.

resources.name: Citizens’ line for people with disabilities (Bürgertelefon)
resources.org: Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (BMAS)
resources.what: The federal labour ministry’s information line for questions about disability. Deaf people can reach the ministry in German Sign Language through its sign-language video phone, or by email at info.gehoerlos@bmas.bund.de.
resources.how: Call Monday to Thursday, 8:00 to 17:00, or Friday, 8:00 to 12:00. The line is in German.

resources.name: Independent participation counselling (EUTB)
resources.org: Ergänzende unabhängige Teilhabeberatung, funded by BMAS
resources.what: Free counselling centres across Germany for disabled people, people at risk of disability and their families. Advisers, some of them disabled, help with money, living independently, wheelchairs and other aids, interpreters and taking part in community life. The centres are not run by service providers, and they do not take on court cases.
resources.how: Find the centre nearest you on teilhabeberatung.de. Counselling is in German; the ministry publishes a brochure about it in English.

resources.name: Severe disability ID card (Schwerbehindertenausweis)
resources.org: Versorgungsamt (disability assessment office) where you live
resources.what: The office assesses your degree of disability (Grad der Behinderung, GdB). With a GdB of at least 50 you count as severely disabled and get the ID card. Depending on the conditions, it can mean free local public transport or lower vehicle tax.
resources.how: Apply to the Versorgungsamt for where you live, on its form or online where offered. You sign a release so the office can request your medical records, which costs you nothing. Offices and forms differ by state, and the process is in German.

resources.name: Conciliation Service under the Disability Equality Act (Schlichtungsstelle BGG)
resources.org: Office of the Federal Government Commissioner for Matters relating to Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Free out-of-court conciliation when a federal public body fails on accessibility or discriminates because of a disability, or when you, or you with your service dog, are refused entry to a place open to the public. You do not need a lawyer or proof of your degree of disability. It does not cover state or local authorities, private shops’ accessibility or private-sector job disputes.
resources.how: Apply in writing, through the contact form, or in person by appointment (Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 12:00). Applications by phone are not possible. Its website has pages in English.

countries.name: France

emergency.label: European emergency number. In France, 15 is medical emergencies (SAMU), 17 the police and 18 the fire brigade

countries.relay: Deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind or aphasic: contact 114 by text message, video, chat or the urgence 114 app. It is free and open at any hour.

resources.name: 3114: national suicide prevention line
resources.org: Numéro national de prévention du suicide
resources.what: A free line open around the clock anywhere in France, for anyone thinking about suicide and for worried family and friends. Nurses and psychologists trained in crisis care answer, and they can send emergency help with the SAMU when needed.
resources.how: Call 3114. The line is in French.

resources.name: MDPH: departmental disability office
resources.what: Each département has an MDPH, the single place to get information and apply for disability help. Its commission (CDAPH) decides on the AAH allowance, the disability compensation benefit (PCH), the mobility inclusion card and recognition as a disabled worker (RQTH). The MDPH for the département where you have lived for more than three months handles your file.
resources.how: Find your MDPH by postcode in the directory on Mon Parcours Handicap. Many accept applications online. Services are in French.

resources.name: Local support line for disabled people and carers
resources.what: A free line that puts disabled people and carers in touch with local advice and support on health care, transport, school and housing.
resources.how: Call 0 800 360 360. The line is in French.

resources.name: Allocation aux adultes handicapés (AAH)
resources.org: Decided by the MDPH; paid by the CAF or MSA
resources.what: A monthly allowance for disabled adults with low incomes. You need an incapacity rate of at least 80%, or 50% to 79% with a substantial and lasting barrier to finding work, and you usually need to be 20 or over. The maximum was €1,041.59 a month in mainland France when this was checked.
resources.how: Apply to your MDPH, online where it offers that or by post on the official form. The commission has four months to answer; no answer by then counts as a refusal. In French.

resources.name: Mobility inclusion card for parking (CMI stationnement)
resources.what: Lets you park free and with no time limit in public on-street spaces, and use disabled parking spaces, as driver or passenger. It is for people whose walking is very limited (for example, under 200 metres) or who need someone with them to get around because of a mental, cognitive, psychiatric or visual impairment, lasting at least a year. The card is free.
resources.how: Under 60, apply to your MDPH on form Cerfa 15692 with ID, proof of address and a medical certificate. At 60 or over, ask for it in your APA application. The old parking card stays valid until 31 December 2026. In French.

resources.name: Défenseur des droits
resources.what: The independent rights authority defends people free of charge when their rights are not respected, including disability discrimination at work, in housing and at school. Disability is one of the most common reasons people turn to it.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 19:30, use the online form, or book a free meeting with one of its local delegates. For discrimination, its platform also answers on 3928 (local rate, weekdays 9:30 to 19:00) and by chat; deaf people can use the Acceo service. In French.

emergency.label: Any emergency, including when a life is in danger

resources.name: 024: line for suicidal behaviour
resources.what: A free, confidential national line, open 24 hours a day, every day, for anyone thinking about suicide and for family and friends. Its professionals listen, give emotional support and refer you to health services, or to 112 in an emergency.
resources.how: Call 024. The line is in Spanish. Deaf callers can reach it in Spanish Sign Language through the SVisual video interpreting service.

resources.name: Recognised degree of disability (certificado de discapacidad)
resources.org: Your autonomous community; IMSERSO in Ceuta and Melilla
resources.what: A team assesses your disability and gives it a percentage. A degree of 33% or more is what counts as having a disability for things like income tax relief. The recognised degree is valid across Spain.
resources.how: Apply to the department in charge in your autonomous community, in person, by post or online. In Ceuta and Melilla, apply to the IMSERSO regional office. In Spanish.

resources.name: Non-contributory invalidity pension (PNC de invalidez)
resources.org: Run by the autonomous communities; rules set by IMSERSO
resources.what: A pension for people aged 18 to 64 with a disability or chronic illness of 65% or more, who have lived legally in Spain for five years (the last two in a row) and do not have enough income. In 2025 the full amount was €564.70 a month. People with 75% or more who need another person’s help get a supplement.
resources.how: Apply to the social services of your autonomous community, which manages the pension. In Spanish.

resources.name: Parking card for people with reduced mobility
resources.what: Lets people with a disability and reduced mobility park in reserved spaces anywhere in Spain; a card from any region is valid nationwide. A one-year provisional card exists for people with a very serious illness who cannot wait for an assessment.
resources.how: Ask the public administration that issues the card where you live. In Spanish.

resources.name: Office for Disability Care (OADIS)
resources.what: Advises on and studies complaints from disabled people about discrimination in public administration, goods and services open to the public, buildings and streets, transport, cultural heritage or the justice system, when the problem reaches two or more autonomous communities. It does not cover employment, dependency benefits or matters already in court.
resources.how: Send your complaint or question in writing through the online form. In Spanish.

resources.name: CERMI: Spanish Committee of Representatives of Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: The national platform that speaks for disabled people in Spain, with more than 800 member organisations. It offers legal guidance to disabled people, their families and organisations that meet its requirements.
resources.how: Call or email to ask about legal guidance. In Spanish.

countries.name: Italy

emergency.label: Any emergency. The older numbers still work too: 113 police, 115 fire brigade, 118 ambulance

countries.relay: Deaf: the free 112Sordi service works across Italy, with text chat and location sharing. The free Where ARE U app can also reach 112 by voice call, silent call or chat.

resources.name: Telefono Amico Italia
resources.what: A listening line answered by trained volunteers for anyone who feels alone or distressed, or is thinking about suicide. It is open every day from 9:00 to midnight, not 24 hours. You can also write on WhatsApp.
resources.how: Call 02 2327 2327; the service is free and you pay only the normal cost of the call. Or message 324 011 7252 on WhatsApp. In Italian.

resources.name: Civil invalidity recognition (invalidità civile)
resources.what: Recognition of civil invalidity is the first step to Italy’s disability payments, such as the monthly allowance for partly disabled people aged 18 to 67 with low incomes. The application and your doctor’s medical certificate go to INPS online.
resources.how: Ask your doctor for the medical certificate, then apply online to INPS. For help with INPS online services, call its contact centre. In Italian.
resources.phone_note: INPS contact centre. Its other number is 06 164 164.

resources.name: European disabled parking permit (CUDE)
resources.what: Lets the holder use disabled parking, and is valid across Italy and in the European Union. It is for people whose walking ability is seriously reduced, and for blind people.
resources.how: Get a certificate from the forensic medicine office of your local health authority (ASL), then apply to your town council (Comune). Permanent permits last five years. In Italian.

resources.name: National Authority for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
resources.org: Autorità Garante nazionale dei diritti delle persone con disabilità
resources.what: An independent national authority set up in 2024. Its work includes countering direct and indirect discrimination against disabled people. In 2025 it took up more than 1,300 reports, mostly about school.
resources.how: See its website for how to send a report. In Italian.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.relay: Deaf, hard of hearing or speech-impaired: text 112 at any hour through the relay service, use the Tolkcontact app, or chat with the control room in the 112NL app. To text 112 directly, register once by texting “aanmelden” to 112.

resources.name: 113 Suicide Prevention (113 Zelfmoordpreventie)
resources.what: Free, anonymous help around the clock for anyone thinking about suicide. It also offers help online.
resources.how: Call 113. The service is in Dutch.

resources.name: Support from your municipality (Wmo)
resources.what: Under the Social Support Act (Wmo 2015), your municipality must help if you cannot manage on your own or take part in society and the people around you cannot help. Support can include a wheelchair for long-term use, regional transport, home adaptations such as a stairlift, household help and respite care. Some support has a personal contribution.
resources.how: Contact your municipality. It works out with you what you need, usually in a conversation. You can take the support as a personal budget (pgb) and arrange it yourself. In Dutch.

resources.name: Wajong benefit for young disabled people
resources.what: Income for people who can never work because of an illness or disability they had at 18, or that began between 18 and 30 after at least six months of study in the year before. You must live in the Netherlands. UWV assesses whether you can work.
resources.how: Apply to UWV. You cannot apply while living abroad. In Dutch.

resources.name: Disabled parking card (gehandicaptenparkeerkaart)
resources.what: For people who have not been able to walk more than 100 metres on their own, even with a cane or rollator, for at least six months. There are cards for drivers and for passengers who need a driver’s help door to door. It is a European card, valid in all EU countries, for up to five years.
resources.how: Apply to your municipality; a medical examiner decides. If you are not registered with a Dutch municipality, apply to the CBR. Each municipality sets its own fee. In Dutch.

resources.name: Netherlands Institute for Human Rights (College voor de Rechten van de Mens)
resources.org: College voor de Rechten van de Mens
resources.what: The national human rights institute rules on discrimination complaints, including under the law on equal treatment on grounds of disability or chronic illness, for example when a needed adjustment is refused.
resources.how: File a complaint on its complaint form, or call Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 16:00. In Dutch.

resources.name: Support centre for adults in mental crisis (Centrum Wsparcia)
resources.what: A free line, open 24 hours, for adults in a mental or emotional crisis.
resources.how: Call 800 70 2222. You can also call 116 123, the national advice line for people in emotional crisis, also open 24 hours. Both are in Polish.

resources.name: Disability degree certificate (orzeczenie o stopniu niepełnosprawności)
resources.org: District disability assessment team (powiatowy zespół do spraw orzekania o niepełnosprawności)
resources.what: Formal confirmation of disability for people over 16, at a mild, moderate or significant degree. It is the key to many kinds of help, such as care benefits, a parking card, rehabilitation funding, extra leave and transport discounts, though most have extra conditions of their own. The service is free.
resources.how: Have your doctor fill in the medical certificate, then take the application and your medical records to the team for where you live. You will be invited to an assessment, and the decision usually comes within 14 days of it. You can appeal within 14 days. In Polish.

resources.name: PFRON funding for orthopaedic items, aids and rehabilitation equipment
resources.org: PFRON, through district family support centres (PCPR)
resources.what: Helps pay for orthopaedic items, aids and rehabilitation equipment, on top of the National Health Fund (NFZ) refund, for people with a disability certificate. Household income must be below set limits: 50% of the average wage per person, or 65% for someone living alone.
resources.how: Apply to your district family support centre (PCPR) with a prescription, a price quote showing the NFZ share and proof of income. In Warsaw, apply to the city’s centre for disabled people. In Polish.

resources.name: Parking card (karta parkingowa)
resources.what: Lets you use disabled parking spaces in Poland and abroad. Your disability certificate must include the right to a parking card; with a moderate degree, it must carry code 04-O, 05-R or 10-N. The card costs 21 zł and lasts as long as your certificate, up to five years.
resources.how: Apply in person to your district or city disability assessment team with your final certificate, a 35 × 45 mm photo and proof of payment. In Polish.

resources.name: Commissioner for Human Rights (Rzecznik Praw Obywatelskich)
resources.what: Checks whether public institutions respect your rights, and handles complaints about unequal treatment, including on grounds of disability. It also monitors how Poland applies the UN disability convention. Complaints are free.
resources.how: Call the free citizens’ helpline from any phone in Poland, use the online complaint form, or email biurorzecznika@brpo.gov.pl. In Polish.

emergency.label: Ambulance (SAMU), free from any phone at any hour

resources.name: CVV (Centro de Valorização da Vida)
resources.what: Emotional support and suicide prevention, 24 hours a day, from trained volunteers. Calls are free under an agreement with the Ministry of Health. You can also chat online.
resources.how: Call 188. In Portuguese.

resources.name: BPC: continuous cash benefit for disabled people (BPC/LOAS)
resources.what: Pays one minimum wage a month to disabled people whose family income is no more than a quarter of the minimum wage per person. You do not need to have paid into INSS. It is for Brazilians and Portuguese nationals, and your CadÚnico registration must have been updated in the last two years. There is no 13th payment.
resources.how: Apply in the Meu INSS app or at gov.br/meuinss. If the system is down, or to book an in-person visit, call 135. Applying is free. In Portuguese.

resources.name: Digital parking credential for disabled people
resources.what: Lets you use parking spaces reserved for disabled people anywhere in Brazil. The credential is now issued digitally in the Carteira Digital de Trânsito (CDT) app, and can be linked to one vehicle at a time, yours or someone else’s.
resources.how: In the CDT app, go to Condutor, then Credencial de Estacionamento, then Credencial PCD, and tap Emitir Credencial. Your disability is checked against Ministry of Human Rights and INSS records. In Portuguese.

resources.name: Disque 100 (Human Rights Line)
resources.org: Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship
resources.what: A free line, open 24 hours every day, for reporting human rights violations, including against disabled people.
resources.how: Dial 100 free from any phone, or send a WhatsApp message to +55 61 99611-0100. There is also a video service in Libras (Brazilian Sign Language). In Portuguese.

emergency.label: Police and ambulance. Fire brigade: 100. In the City of Buenos Aires and parts of Buenos Aires Province, 107 is the SAME ambulance

resources.name: National mental health urgent support line
resources.org: Ministerio de Salud de la Nación
resources.what: A free, confidential line open 24 hours every day across the country, answered by trained mental health professionals. It helps with suicide risk, self-harm and crises linked to substance use, violence or disasters, and can send emergency services.
resources.how: Call 0800 999 0091. In Spanish. The government also lists 135 as a suicide prevention line.

resources.name: Certificado Único de Discapacidad (CUD)
resources.what: A free national document certifying disability, issued after an assessment by an interdisciplinary board. It gives access to full coverage of rehabilitation linked to the disability, free travel on public ground transport, family allowances and some tax and toll exemptions.
resources.how: Gather your medical reports, use the online check to see what to bring and where to go, book an appointment with the evaluation board, then collect the CUD in person. It also appears in the Mi Argentina app. In Spanish.

resources.name: Non-contributory pension for work disability (pensión no contributiva por invalidez laboral)
resources.org: Secretaría Nacional de Discapacidad, applied for through ANSES
resources.what: A pension for people with a total and permanent disability (work capacity reduced by 66% or more) who have no other pension or registered job and not enough income. Foreign residents need 10 years of residence. Applying is free; do not pay agents or lawyers to do it.
resources.how: Get the digital official medical certificate (CMO) at a public hospital or health centre, then apply in Mi ANSES or at an ANSES office. Check on your case on WhatsApp at +54 11 3910-1010. In Spanish.

resources.name: International Symbol of Access for vehicles
resources.what: A free digital symbol, linked to a number plate, for the vehicle a person with a valid CUD travels in. It lets that vehicle drive and park under each town’s traffic rules. You do not need to own a car.
resources.how: Request it in Mi Argentina, under Mis Trámites, with your CUD and the plate number. Questions go to simbolos@senadis.gob.ar. In Spanish.

resources.name: Línea 106 mental health line
resources.org: Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social
resources.what: A free, confidential line open 24 hours, 7 days a week. Mental health professionals listen, give first support and point you to help.
resources.how: Dial 106 from a landline or mobile. Video calls can also be booked. In Spanish.

resources.name: Disability certification (certificación de discapacidad)
resources.org: Ministerio de Salud; requested through your municipal or district health secretariat
resources.what: A team of health and social professionals assesses you and issues a disability certificate, and your details go into the national register of disabled people (RLCPD).
resources.how: Ask your municipal or district health secretariat for a certification order, with your medical history and diagnosis from your treating doctor. The secretariat checks your papers within about four working days, and the assessing clinic must schedule you within 10 working days. For questions, call the Ministry. In Spanish.
resources.phone_note: Ministry of Health, toll-free from outside Bogotá

resources.name: Defensoría del Pueblo
resources.what: The national ombudsman takes complaints, free of charge, about human rights violations by public officials or service providers.
resources.how: Call the national toll-free line, or use the online services on its website. In Spanish.

resources.name: *4141 Suicide Prevention Line
resources.what: A free line, open 24 hours, Monday to Sunday, for anyone in a mental health crisis linked to suicide, including suicidal thoughts, intense emotional pain, panic or wanting to self-harm. A psychologist answers.
resources.how: Dial *4141 from a mobile phone on any network. In Spanish.

resources.name: National Disability Register and disability credential
resources.what: COMPIN assesses and certifies your disability, then the Registro Civil enters you in the National Disability Register (RND) and issues a credential. Registration is free. It opens the door to SENADIS programmes, reserved parking, housing subsidies, job inclusion benefits and more.
resources.how: Apply online at compin.cerofilas.gob.cl with your RUT and ClaveÚnica, or at your local COMPIN office, with the medical and social reports it asks for. COMPIN aims to decide in about 20 working days. In Spanish.

resources.name: SENADIS assistive devices programme (Programa Regular de Ayudas Técnicas)
resources.what: Pays for up to two assistive devices for disabled people aged 10 and over who are on the National Disability Register and in the most vulnerable 70% of the Registro Social de Hogares. It opens in yearly calls; the 2026 call closed on 7 April 2026.
resources.how: Watch for the next call, or email the programme. In Spanish.

resources.name: Línea 113 Salud, option 5 (mental health)
resources.what: A free mental health line open 24 hours every day across the country, answered by psychologists experienced in emotional crises.
resources.how: Call 113 and choose option 5. You can also write on WhatsApp or Telegram to 955 557 000. In Spanish.

resources.name: Disability certificate and CONADIS registration card
resources.org: Ministry of Health centres and CONADIS
resources.what: First get a disability certificate from a health centre certified by the Ministry of Health; some tests may cost money. Then register with CONADIS, the national authority on disability, for its card, which unlocks benefits such as free public transport for severe disability and a vehicle sticker.
resources.how: Register online on the CONADIS platform by uploading your certificate. You get a digital card by email, and can collect a printed one in Lima or at a regional office. In Spanish.

resources.name: Contigo pension for severe disability
resources.org: Programa Nacional Contigo (Ministry of Development and Social Inclusion)
resources.what: A pension for people with a severe disability living in poverty or extreme poverty who have no other income or pension, public or private.
resources.how: You need a disability certificate rated severe from a Ministry of Health centre and a current poverty rating, which you request from your district municipality. Your district’s OMAPED office can check whether you are enrolled. Payments are collected at Banco de la Nación. In Spanish.
